verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 22.89
verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.89

verses.pali: 9. Theravagga
verses.english: 9. Senior Mendicants

verses.pali: Khemakasutta
verses.english: With Khemaka

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ sambahulā therā bhikkhū kosambiyaṁ viharanti ghositārāme.
verses.english: At one time several senior mendicants were staying near Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā khemako badarikārāme viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Khemaka was staying in the Jujube Tree Monastery, and he was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho therā bhikkhū sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitā āyasmantaṁ dāsakaṁ āmantesuṁ:
verses.english: In the late afternoon those senior mendicants came out of retreat and addressed Venerable Dāsaka,

verses.pali: “ehi tvaṁ, āvuso dāsaka, yena khemako bhikkhu tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā khemakaṁ bhikkhuṁ evaṁ vadehi:
verses.english: “Please, Reverend Dāsaka, go to the mendicant Khemaka and say to him:

verses.pali: ‘therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu—
verses.english: ‘Reverend Khemaka, the seniors

verses.pali: kacci te, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ, kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti no abhikkamanti, paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no abhikkamo’”ti?
verses.english: hope you’re keeping well; they hope you’re all right. They hope that your pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā dāsako therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paṭissutvā yenāyasmā khemako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ khemakaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: “Yes, reverends,” replied Dāsaka. He went to Khemaka and said to him:

verses.pali: “therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu:
verses.english: “Reverend Khemaka, the seniors

verses.pali: ‘kacci te, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ …pe… no abhikkamo’”ti?
verses.english: hope you’re keeping well; they hope you’re all right. They hope that your pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

verses.pali: “Na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ …pe… abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo”ti.
verses.english: “Reverend, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā dāsako yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Dāsaka went to those senior mendicants and told them what had happened. They said,

verses.pali: “khemako, āvuso, bhikkhu evamāha:
‘na me, āvuso, khamanīyaṁ …pe… abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati no paṭikkamo’”ti.
“Ehi tvaṁ, āvuso dāsaka, yena khemako bhikkhu tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā khemakaṁ bhikkhuṁ evaṁ vadehi:
verses.english: “Please, Reverend Dāsaka, go to the mendicant Khemaka and say to him:

verses.pali: ‘therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu—
verses.english: ‘Reverend Khemaka, the seniors say that

verses.pali: pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: these five grasping aggregates have been taught by the Buddha, that is:

verses.pali: rūpupādānakkhandho, vedanupādānakkhandho, saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
verses.english: the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: Imesu āyasmā khemako pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassatī’”ti?
verses.english: Do you regard anything among these five grasping aggregates as self or as belonging to self?’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā dāsako therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paṭissutvā yenāyasmā khemako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā …pe…
verses.english: “Yes, reverends,” replied Dāsaka. He relayed the message to Khemaka, who replied:

verses.pali: therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu:
“pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
Imesu āyasmā khemako pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassatī”ti?
“Pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: “These five grasping aggregates have been taught by the Buddha, that is:

verses.pali: rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
verses.english: the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: Imesu khvāhaṁ, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu na kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassāmī”ti.
verses.english: I do not regard anything among these five grasping aggregates as self or as belonging to self.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā dāsako yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā there bhikkhū etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Dāsaka went to those senior mendicants and told them what had happened. They said:

verses.pali: “khemako, āvuso, bhikkhu evamāha:
‘pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
Imesu khvāhaṁ, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu na kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassāmī’”ti.
“Ehi tvaṁ, āvuso dāsaka, yena khemako bhikkhu tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā khemakaṁ bhikkhuṁ evaṁ vadehi:
verses.english: “Please, Reverend Dāsaka, go to the mendicant Khemaka and say to him:

verses.pali: ‘therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu—
verses.english: ‘Reverend Khemaka, the seniors say that

verses.pali: pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: these five grasping aggregates have been taught by the Buddha, that is:

verses.pali: rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
verses.english: the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: No ce kirāyasmā khemako imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassati.
verses.english: If, as it seems, Venerable Khemaka does not regard anything among these five grasping aggregates as self or as belonging to self,

verses.pali: Tenahāyasmā khemako arahaṁ khīṇāsavo’”ti.
verses.english: then he is a perfected one, with defilements ended.’”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā dāsako therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paṭissutvā yenāyasmā khemako …pe…
verses.english: “Yes, reverends,” replied Dāsaka. He relayed the message to Khemaka, who replied:

verses.pali: therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu:
“pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho;
no ce kirāyasmā khemako imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassati, tenahāyasmā khemako arahaṁ khīṇāsavo”ti.
“Pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
verses.english: “These five grasping aggregates have been taught by the Buddha, that is:

verses.pali: rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
verses.english: the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: Imesu khvāhaṁ, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu na kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassāmi, na camhi arahaṁ khīṇāsavo;
verses.english: I do not regard anything among these five grasping aggregates as self or as belonging to self, yet I am not a perfected one, with defilements ended.

verses.pali: api ca me, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu ‘asmī’ti adhigataṁ, ‘ayamahamasmī’ti na ca samanupassāmī”ti.
verses.english: For when it comes to the five grasping aggregates I’m not rid of the conceit ‘I am’. But I don’t regard anything as ‘I am this’.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā dāsako yena therā bhikkhū …pe…
verses.english: Then Dāsaka went to those senior mendicants and told them what had happened. They said:

verses.pali: there bhikkhū etadavoca:
“khemako, āvuso, bhikkhu evamāha—
pañcime, āvuso, upādānakkhandhā vuttā bhagavatā, seyyathidaṁ—
rūpupādānakkhandho …pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho.
Imesu khvāhaṁ, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu na kiñci attaṁ vā attaniyaṁ vā samanupassāmi, na camhi arahaṁ khīṇāsavo;
api ca me, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu ‘asmī’ti adhigataṁ, ‘ayamahamasmī’ti na ca samanupassāmī”ti.
“Ehi tvaṁ, āvuso dāsaka, yena khemako bhikkhu tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā khemakaṁ bhikkhuṁ evaṁ vadehi:
verses.english: “Please, Reverend Dāsaka, go to the mendicant Khemaka and say to him:

verses.pali: ‘therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu—
verses.english: ‘Reverend Khemaka, the seniors ask,

verses.pali: yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, asmīti vadesi, kimetaṁ asmīti vadesi?
verses.english: when you say “I am”, what is it that you’re talking about?

verses.pali: Rūpaṁ asmīti vadesi, aññatra rūpā asmīti vadesi,
verses.english: Is it form or apart from form?

verses.pali: vedanaṁ …
verses.english: Is it feeling …

verses.pali: saññaṁ …
verses.english: perception …

verses.pali: saṅkhāre …
verses.english: choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ asmīti vadesi, aññatra viññāṇā asmīti vadesi.
verses.english: consciousness, or apart from consciousness?

verses.pali: Yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, asmīti vadesi. Kimetaṁ asmīti vadesī’”ti?
verses.english: When you say “I am”, what is it that you’re talking about?”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā dāsako therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ paṭissutvā yenāyasmā khemako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ khemakaṁ etadavoca—
verses.english: “Yes, reverends,” replied Dāsaka. He relayed the message to Khemaka, who replied:

verses.pali: therā taṁ, āvuso khemaka, evamāhaṁsu:
“yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, ‘asmī’ti vadesi, kimetaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
Rūpaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi aññatra rūpā ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
Vedanaṁ …
saññaṁ …
saṅkhāre …
viññāṇaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi aññatra viññāṇā ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
Yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, ‘asmī’ti vadesi, kimetaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesī”ti?
“Alaṁ, āvuso dāsaka, kiṁ imāya sandhāvanikāya.
verses.english: “Enough, Reverend Dāsaka! What’s the point in running back and forth?

verses.pali: Āharāvuso, daṇḍaṁ;
verses.english: Bring my staff,

verses.pali: ahameva yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkamissāmī”ti.
verses.english: I’ll go to see the senior mendicants myself.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā khemako daṇḍamolubbha yena therā bhikkhū tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā therehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then Venerable Khemaka, leaning on a staff, went to those senior mendicants and exchanged greetings with them.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ khemakaṁ therā bhikkhū etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. They said to him:

verses.pali: “yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, ‘asmī’ti vadesi, kimetaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
verses.english: “Reverend Khemaka, when you say ‘I am’, what is it that you’re talking about?

verses.pali: Rūpaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi, aññatra rūpā ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
verses.english: Is it form or apart from form?

verses.pali: Vedanaṁ …
verses.english: Is it feeling …

verses.pali: saññaṁ …
verses.english: perception …

verses.pali: saṅkhāre …
verses.english: choices …

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesi, aññatra viññāṇā ‘asmī’ti vadesi?
verses.english: consciousness, or apart from consciousness?

verses.pali: Yametaṁ, āvuso khemaka, ‘asmī’ti vadesi, kimetaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadesī”ti?
verses.english: When you say ‘I am’, what is it that you’re talking about?”

verses.pali: “Na khvāhaṁ, āvuso, rūpaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadāmi; napi aññatra rūpā ‘asmī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: “Reverends, I don’t say ‘I am’ with reference to form, or apart from form.

verses.pali: Na vedanaṁ …
verses.english: I don’t say ‘I am’ with reference to feeling …

verses.pali: na saññaṁ …
verses.english: perception …

verses.pali: na saṅkhāre …
verses.english: choices …

verses.pali: na viññāṇaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadāmi; napi aññatra viññāṇā ‘asmī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: consciousness, or apart from consciousness.

verses.pali: Api ca me, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu ‘asmī’ti adhigataṁ ‘ayamahamasmī’ti na ca samanupassāmi.
verses.english: For when it comes to the five grasping aggregates I’m not rid of the conceit ‘I am’. But I don’t regard anything as ‘I am this’.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, uppalassa vā padumassa vā puṇḍarīkassa vā gandho.
verses.english: It’s like the scent of a blue water lily, or a pink or white lotus.

verses.pali: Yo nu kho evaṁ vadeyya: ‘pattassa gandho’ti vā ‘vaṇṇassa gandho’ti vā ‘kiñjakkhassa gandho’ti vā sammā nu kho so vadamāno vadeyyā”ti?
verses.english: Would it be right to say that the scent belongs to the petals or the stalk or the pistil?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “No, reverend.”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ, panāvuso, sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā”ti?
verses.english: “Then, reverends, how should it be said?”

verses.pali: “‘Pupphassa gandho’ti kho, āvuso, sammā byākaramāno byākareyyā”ti.
verses.english: “It would be right to say that the scent belongs to the flower.”

verses.pali: “Evameva khvāhaṁ, āvuso, na rūpaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadāmi, napi aññatra rūpā ‘asmī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: “In the same way, reverends, I don’t say ‘I am’ with reference to form, or apart from form.

verses.pali: Na vedanaṁ …
verses.english: I don’t say ‘I am’ with reference to feeling …

verses.pali: na saññaṁ …
verses.english: perception …

verses.pali: na saṅkhāre …
verses.english: choices …

verses.pali: na viññāṇaṁ ‘asmī’ti vadāmi, napi aññatra viññāṇā ‘asmī’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: consciousness, or apart from consciousness.

verses.pali: Api ca me, āvuso, pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu ‘asmī’ti adhigataṁ ‘ayamahamasmī’ti na ca samanupassāmi.
verses.english: For when it comes to the five grasping aggregates I’m not rid of the conceit ‘I am’. But I don’t regard anything as ‘I am this’.

verses.pali: Kiñcāpi, āvuso, ariyasāvakassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni bhavanti, atha khvassa hoti: ‘yo ca pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anusahagato asmīti māno, asmīti chando, asmīti anusayo asamūhato.
verses.english: Although a noble disciple has given up the five lower fetters, they still have a lingering residue of the conceit ‘I am’, the desire ‘I am’, and the underlying tendency ‘I am’ which has not been eradicated.

verses.pali: So aparena samayena pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassī viharati—
verses.english: After some time they meditate observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā …
verses.english: Such is feeling …

verses.pali: iti saññā …
verses.english: Such is perception …

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā …
verses.english: Such are choices …

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

verses.pali: Tassimesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassino viharato yopissa hoti pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anusahagato ‘asmī’ti, māno ‘asmī’ti, chando ‘asmī’ti anusayo asamūhato, sopi samugghātaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: As they do so, that lingering residue is eradicated.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso, vatthaṁ saṅkiliṭṭhaṁ malaggahitaṁ. Tamenaṁ sāmikā rajakassa anupadajjuṁ.
verses.english: Suppose there was a cloth that was dirty and soiled, so the owners give it to a launderer.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ rajako ūse vā khāre vā gomaye vā sammadditvā acche udake vikkhāleti.
verses.english: The launderer kneads it thoroughly with salt, lye, and cow dung, and rinses it in clear water.

verses.pali: Kiñcāpi taṁ hoti vatthaṁ parisuddhaṁ pariyodātaṁ, atha khvassa hoti yeva anusahagato ūsagandho vā khāragandho vā gomayagandho vā asamūhato.
verses.english: Although that cloth is clean and bright, it still has a lingering scent of salt, lye, or cow dung that had not been eradicated.

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ rajako sāmikānaṁ deti. Tamenaṁ sāmikā gandhaparibhāvite karaṇḍake nikkhipanti.
verses.english: The launderer returns it to its owners, who store it in a fragrant casket.

verses.pali: Yopissa hoti anusahagato ūsagandho vā khāragandho vā gomayagandho vā asamūhato, sopi samugghātaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: And that lingering scent would be eradicated.

verses.pali: Evameva kho, āvuso, kiñcāpi ariyasāvakassa pañcorambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni bhavanti, atha khvassa hoti yeva pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anusahagato ‘asmī’ti, māno ‘asmī’ti, chando ‘asmī’ti anusayo asamūhato.
verses.english: In the same way, although a noble disciple has given up the five lower fetters, they still have a lingering residue of the conceit ‘I am’, the desire ‘I am’, and the underlying tendency ‘I am’ which has not been eradicated.

verses.pali: So aparena samayena pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassī viharati.
verses.english: After some time they meditate observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: ‘Iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā …
verses.english: Such is feeling …

verses.pali: iti saññā …
verses.english: Such is perception …

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā …
verses.english: Such are choices …

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

verses.pali: Tassa imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassino viharato yopissa hoti pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu anusahagato ‘asmī’ti, māno ‘asmī’ti, chando ‘asmī’ti anusayo asamūhato, sopi samugghātaṁ gacchatī”ti.
verses.english: As they do so, that lingering residue is eradicated.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, therā bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ khemakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When he said this, the senior mendicants said to Venerable Khemaka,

verses.pali: “na kho mayaṁ āyasmantaṁ khemakaṁ vihesāpekhā pucchimha, api cāyasmā khemako pahosi tassa bhagavato sāsanaṁ vitthārena ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
verses.english: “We didn’t want to trouble Venerable Khemaka with our questions. But you’re capable of explaining, teaching, asserting, establishing, clarifying, analyzing, and revealing the Buddha’s instructions in detail.

verses.pali: Tayidaṁ āyasmatā khemakena tassa bhagavato sāsanaṁ vitthārena ācikkhitaṁ desitaṁ paññāpitaṁ paṭṭhapitaṁ vivaritaṁ vibhajitaṁ uttānīkatan”ti.
verses.english: And that’s just what you’ve done.”

verses.pali: Idamavoca āyasmā khemako.
verses.english: That’s what Venerable Khemaka said.

verses.pali: Attamanā therā bhikkhū āyasmato khemakassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanduṁ.
verses.english: Satisfied, the senior mendicants approved what Venerable Khemaka said.

verses.pali: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne saṭṭhimattānaṁ therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṁsu, āyasmato khemakassa cāti.
verses.english: And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of sixty senior mendicants and of Venerable Khemaka were freed from defilements by not grasping.

verses.pali: Sattamaṁ.
